guide.summary: Unit 2 covers decision making and repetition: boolean expressions, relational and logical operators, if/else-if/else, nested conditionals, De Morgan's laws and equivalent expressions, comparing objects, while and for loops, String traversal, nested loops, standard loop algorithms, and counting loop iterations.

sections.heading: Boolean expressions and conditionals
sections.body: Relational operators (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=) produce booleans; logical operators combine them: && (and), || (or), ! (not). Java short-circuits: in a && b, b isn't evaluated if a is false; in a || b, b isn't evaluated if a is true (useful for guarding against division by zero or null). De Morgan's laws: !(a && b) is !a || !b; !(a || b) is !a && !b. The negation of x > 5 is x <= 5. In an if/else-if chain, only the first true branch runs. Compare object content with equals; == compares references.

sections.heading: Loops
sections.body: A while loop repeats while its condition is true; make sure the condition eventually becomes false to avoid infinite loops. A for loop has initialization, condition, and update: for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) runs n times. A loop that changes i by a factor (i *= 2) runs about log₂ n times. Off-by-one errors come from using <= vs. < incorrectly. Standard algorithms: sum or average, count items meeting a condition, find max/min (initialize with the first value or Integer.MIN_VALUE), check whether any/all items meet a condition, process digits with % 10 and / 10, and determine primes or divisors.

sections.heading: String traversal and nested loops
sections.body: Traverse a String with for (int i = 0; i < str.length(); i++) and access one-character substrings with str.substring(i, i + 1). To reverse, loop from str.length() − 1 down to 0. For substrings of length k, loop i from 0 to str.length() − k. Nested loops repeat the inner loop fully for each outer iteration; total executions multiply (or sum, if the inner bound depends on the outer variable, e.g., 4 + 3 + 2 + 1).

keyTakeaways: Short-circuit evaluation can prevent runtime errors.
De Morgan: flip operators and negate each part.
for (i = 0; i < n; i++) → n iterations.
Nested loops: count inner executions carefully.
Only the first true branch of an else-if chain runs.
commonMistakes: Negating x > 5 as x < 5 (should be x <= 5).
Off-by-one with str.length() as an index.
Forgetting to update the loop variable in a while loop.
examTips: Count iterations with a small table of loop variable values.
For equivalence questions, test with a few sample values, including boundaries.
In FRQs, initialize accumulators before loops and return after them.
Check that your loop works for empty or single-character Strings.
guide.cramSheet:
**Booleans:** && || ! · short-circuit · De Morgan !(a && b) = !a || !b

**Conditionals:** first true branch only · equals for objects

**Loops:** for n times · while until false · i *= 2 → log n

**Algorithms:** sum, count, max/min, any/all, digits (% 10, / 10)

**Strings:** substring(i, i + 1) · reverse from length() − 1 · windows to length() − k

**Nested:** multiply (or sum if dependent)

practice.prompt:
Write two static methods in a class NumberTools.

(a) `digitalRoot(int n)` returns the result of repeatedly summing the digits of n until a single digit remains. For example, digitalRoot(9875) returns 2 (9 + 8 + 7 + 5 = 29, 2 + 9 = 11, 1 + 1 = 2). Assume n ≥ 0.

(b) `longestRun(String str)` returns the length of the longest run of consecutive identical characters in str. For example, longestRun("aabbbcc") returns 3 and longestRun("abc") returns 1. Assume str has length at least 1.

rubric.description: Correctly sums digits using % 10 and / 10 in an inner loop.
Updates n to the digit sum each pass and returns the single digit.
Compares each character with the previous one without going out of bounds.
Increments the current run when characters match; resets to 1 otherwise.
Tracks the maximum run length, including a run at the end of the String.
